issues.detail: The agent loop implements only a subset of member tools (no zoom, drag, triple_click, hold_key) and leaves run_other_tool and screenshot downscaling unimplemented, and the approval helper is never wired into the loop and relies on a crude keyword match on the task text.

The skill is tied to the Anthropic API and Claude-specific toolset versions and beta headers, and the code assumes a Linux/Xvfb desktop with scrot, so it does not carry over to other agents or operating systems.

scenarios.name: agent-loop-batch-failure-handling
scenarios.rationale: A answers every block, echoes toolset_name 'computer', runs in order, halts at the first failure with an is_error 'Not executed' text for the rest, and dispatches on call.name rather than input.action, so it covers all four rubric points; B answers every block and halts after a failure, but it never echoes toolset_name, dispatches on block.input, uses a 'Skipped' message, and calls the old computer_20250124 tool type, while also saying later actions can still run.

scenarios.name: declare-current-toolset-and-migrate
scenarios.rationale: B covers every rubric point: the new toolset type, no beta header, rejected display parameters, dispatch on name plus toolset_name, honoring repeat on key, resizing screenshots yourself, and zoom on by default with the configs disable. A omits the repeat field and never says to resize screenshots, though it does cover the declaration, beta header, rejected parameters, dispatch and zoom.

scenarios.name: safe-sandbox-form-fill-with-approval
scenarios.rationale: A matches more of the rubric: it recommends a sandbox, a max_steps cap, a per-call approval gate that prompts on clicks, and a task prompt that screenshots after each step and forbids Submit. B has strong guardrails and a good prompt, but it has no throwaway container/VM, no max_steps cap, and no approved() prompt-style human approval; it uses a hook that blocks and a browser guard instead.
